issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to initialize the SealSaloon attributes (orders and stock) in the constructor (no-arg constructor). Later in the same statement it mandates that the stock attribute must be static and shared across all instances. Initializing a static (class) field in an instance constructor is misleading and contradictory: it suggests instance-level initialization while also requiring a class-level (static) field. This can confuse students about where and how to create/initialize the shared stock and whether to make it static or instance-level.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the instructions in the problem statement: explicitly state that the stock field should be declared static (e.g., "private static final Stock stock") and initialized at declaration (or in a static initializer), while orders should be an instance field initialized in the no-arg constructor. Remove or reword the sentence that tells students to initialize the stock in the instance constructor to avoid mixed guidance.
